displayPattern: LED behind the blower-door view port on a York TG9S. Each flash is 1/3 second on and 1/3 second off, then a 2-second pause: 9 red flashes
meaning: Reversed line-voltage polarity, a grounding problem, or reversed low-voltage transformer wires. Heating and cooling are both affected. The furnace will not start the ignition sequence until this is corrected.
causes: Flame probe shorted to the chassis
diySteps: Leave the furnace off if it will not light. Do not swap wires on the furnace
Technician: check polarity at the furnace and the branch circuit, check furnace grounding, and check that the flame probe is not shorted to the chassis
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician. Nine red flashes is an electrical fault, not a filter or vent problem.
